# Nutanix Interview Experience for Tech Support Engineer

Last Updated : 3 Oct, 2023

Nutanix Came to our college in August 2023 as a Tech Support Engineer. There was a total of three rounds.

### Round 1: Technical Assessment

* It was an MCQ assessment on the Hacker rank platform.
* MCQ questions were easy.
* They were regarding Computer Networks, Hardware, Cloud, and Linux Operating Systems.

### Round 2: Technical Round

In the second round, the interviewer asked me to follow questions.

* Tell me about you.
* Do you like hardware or software?
* What /etc/hosts/files do in Linux?
* What are the services that Windows provides?
* If one PC is not being powered on, how do you power on that PC?
* How will you pass data through a system that is not working?

After seeing my resume, the interviewer also asked me If your resume is towards development then why

title: One Site Unreachable From One PC
reported: nutanix.com works on one machine but not another on the same network while other sites work; troubleshoot (DNS cache, then discover a patch rewrote /etc/hosts).

cannot answer any in depth questions anymore then the interviewer will switch to another topic and start this process again.

Tips: Make sure you know one technology very well and have extensive knowledge and experience in that. Mine was Linux, can be anything only related to the required skills.

### Round 3, Technical Round 2:

This round is a Version 2 of the first round. on every topic there are going to be more advanced questions, more in depth troubleshooting questions. Questions arise from the topics which were not covered in Technical Round 1.

Examples of questions :

* I can access the website nutanix.com from one computer in a network. But i cannot access the same site from another computer in the same network. However other sites were working, except this specific site . How will you troubleshoot this?

I went through all the regular steps of DNS cache flushing and renewing the cache. however this problem was not resolved. You can probe the interviewer about how this situation arose and what they were doing before this problem occured.

The interviewer (posing as a client ) had run some system security patches after which this occured.

The answer after a lot of questions back and forth was that the security patched had changed the /etc/hosts file explicitly to point nutanix.com to a wrong IP address. Resetting the change fixed this issue.   
  
These kind of questions are common , questions change drastically depending on your skillset and expertise.

Fifteen days after the online assessment, I received an email from PayPal inviting me to the next round of interviews, which was a technical interview.

The technical interview began with a brief and formal introduction. The interviewer then proceeded to ask questions about data structures, their time complexities, and various use cases. Additionally, questions on object-oriented programming (OOP) concepts and some basic development knowledge were also posed.

* Data Structures: The questions covered arrays, linked lists, trees, and graphs. I was asked to explain their time complexities and typical use cases.
* OOP Concepts: The interviewer asked about inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, and abstraction.
* Development: There were a few questions about my experience with software development, particularly focusing on any projects I had listed on my resume.

The coding challenge in this interview was of easy to medium difficulty. I was asked to solve a problem and then discuss potential optimizations. Although I managed to solve the problem, my knowledge of code optimization wasn't as strong, and I struggled to provide an optimized solution.
